settings.heading: Honor in everything we do.
settings.body: We build premium active-lifestyle apparel for people who live with purpose — and we do it in a way we can be proud of, on the trail, on the job, and in the communities we serve.
Honor In Clothing is more than apparel. It represents a commitment to honor, character, purpose, integrity, and legacy — values worth wearing, and worth living.

settings.heading: Our Story
settings.body_1: Honor In Clothing was founded on a simple belief: the way you live matters more than the clothes you wear. In a world where trends change by the season and clothing often becomes disposable, we wanted to create something different — a brand built on timeless values instead of temporary fashion.
settings.body_2: Honor isn't about perfection. It's about character. It's keeping your word when no one is watching. It's showing up for your family, your friends, and your community. It's working hard, taking responsibility, treating others with respect, and leaving places better than you found them. Those principles inspired the creation of Honor In Clothing.

settings.title: Honor
settings.description: Doing what's right even when no one is watching — in our materials, our making, and our word.

settings.title: Character

settings.title: Integrity
settings.description: No shortcuts, no throwaway trends. What we promise is what we deliver.

settings.title: Hard Work

settings.title: Responsibility
settings.description: To our craft, our customers, and the communities and causes we serve.

settings.title: Service
settings.description: Giving back is built into the brand — starting with the veterans who served us all.

settings.title: Legacy
settings.description: Gear designed to be repaired, re-worn, and passed on. Built to outlast the season.

settings.heading: We honor those who served.
settings.body: Honor In Clothing is committed to donating 10% of our annual profits to a carefully vetted organization supporting veterans living with PTSD. This commitment is deeply personal — one of our founders' fathers served our country and struggled with PTSD, and its effects were felt throughout the family for generations. Supporting those who have sacrificed for others is part of what honor means to us.
